title: Adaptive prefetch & clock harmonization for mixed-MIG workloads on H100/A10
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We observe elevated p99 prefill latency on mixed-MIG servers when small, bursty requests (token < 64) land on slices with different clock governors. The router currently selects kernels based on static heuristics and CPU-side prefill is often cold for KV cache on A10 slices. Goal: implement a lightweight adaptive prefetch heuristic in the request router to warm per-slice KV caches for likely short-context requests and add a clock harmonization controller that nudges slice clock governors toward a cooperative operating point for bursty traffic. Scope: (1) router prefetch policy (heuristic + metrics gating), (2) per-MIG harmonizer service (non-privileged control plane agent that recommends clock caps), (3) kernel selection fallback rules (thermal/clock-aware), (4) rollout plan and telemetry. Success metric: reduce p99 prefill+decode latency for small-token workloads by >=15% on mixed H100/A10 hosts without increasing 95th token cost by >5%. Approach / trade-offs: The prefetch will be conservative (prefetch only when request probability score > 0.6 and target slice KV occupancy < 30%) to avoid wasted memory and extra GPU work. Harmonizer will expose recommended clock ceilings via runtime hints; enforcement requires ops approval. We considered fully centralized clock arbitration but rejected it due to blast radius and required privileges; the harmonizer uses advisory hints and relies on existing hw governors where possible. Risks: accidentally increasing power draw during sustained high throughput, and added complexity in kernel selection leading to oscillations. Mitigations: short cooldown windows, sigmoid smoothing on governor hints, and immediate fallback to stable kernel variant under thermal alarms. Deliverables: RFC doc, router runtime change, harmonizer daemon, unit + integration tests, perf dashboard panel, canary rollout script.
acceptance_criteria: New router prefetch policy implements probability scoring and only triggers warm-ups when multiple gating conditions pass
Harmonizer exposes per-slice clock recommendations via the runtime hints API and runtime respects them when allowed by node config
Measured p99 prefill+decode latency improvement >= 15% on mixed H100/A10 test suites for token<=64 workloads
No customer-facing errors or increased error-rate in canary (error rate delta < 0.1%)
Automated test coverage for prefetch gating logic and harmonizer smoothing logic included
Runbook updated with rollback steps and thermal fallback behavior
